questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, chock the wheels and release air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes turn on.

questions.question: On an uphill grade, gravity will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow your vehicle down.
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle down when driving uphill. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: Where must the ABS malfunction lamp be located on a dolly with ABS?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side
questions.explanation: A dolly with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks with manual drains?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every day
questions.explanation: Drain manual air tank drains at the end of each day. This stops oil and water from building up in the air tanks.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely near the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely near the crash and tell police about the aggressive driving.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: When you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect braking distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples.
questions.explanation: Higher speed increases your vehicle's force and braking distance. Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph multiplies your braking distance by four.

questions.question: A distracted driver usually:

options.text: Is aware of what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has slower awareness.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving slows your awareness and reaction time, leading to poor decisions and bad actions. Avoid distracted drivers when you can.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, seeing fresh oil under your vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A problem.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Any of these leaks is a problem before driving.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Grip between the tires and road
The time it takes to use the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip between the tires and road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. You need good traction to brake and steer safely.

questions.question: The service air line is connected to the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Relay valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: When it is hard for other drivers to see your vehicle, such as at dawn or dusk, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights on.
questions.explanation: When visibility is low, turn your headlights on to the low beam setting. If you cannot see others, they probably cannot see you either.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will get out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: Act quickly when your brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will move, and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: What does it mean to have ABS on only one axle?

options.text: It does not change braking in any way.
It gives the driver better control when braking.
It causes extra strain on the other axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives the driver better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) on just one axle still gives the driver better control over the vehicle when braking.

questions.question: What can federal inspectors do if they find your vehicle unsafe?

options.text: Take you to a garage to have your vehicle fixed.
Ask you to have your vehicle's problems fixed.
Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a vehicle unsafe, they can remove it from service until it is fixed.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They are illegal in most states.
They help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved, convex mirrors. They allow drivers to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Get out and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, get out immediately and walk away from the tracks. Contact emergency authorities right away.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Damage to it can be very dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about doubles and triples?

options.text: They can swerve more easily than most other vehicles.
They should be driven 20 mph slower than posted speed limits.
Drivers must identify hazards well in advance.
They should not be driven in the rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must identify hazards well in advance.
questions.explanation: To avoid rolling over and jackknifing, doubles and triples must be driven smoothly. Drivers should look far ahead to spot hazards early and have time to maneuver safely.

questions.question: How should you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal followed by the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
Swerve from side to side to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This tells drivers behind you that you plan to slow down.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before beginning a trip. After making sure the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor and check that the trailer does not move.
